Governed Agentic AI for Banking Fraud Investigation

Four AI agents gather and explain the evidence for every fraud alert. A transparent policy gate routes each case, and people make every decision that affects a customer.

The problem

Banks already detect suspicious transactions well. The slow part is what happens next: an analyst must investigate every alert by hand.

Alerts wait in queues

When alert volumes rise, alerts wait for an analyst, and high-risk cases wait again for a senior investigator.

Evidence is gathered by hand

Analysts switch between core banking, customer profiles, device logs and rule outputs for every single alert.

Decisions are hard to audit

Two analysts can weigh the same evidence differently, and reasons are written in free text that is hard to review.

Our solution

An orchestrator coordinates four specialised agents. Each agent has one narrow job, sees only masked evidence, and can recommend but never act.

Agent 1

Transaction Analysis

Lists the red flags supported by the facts: amount, device, location, time, beneficiary, velocity.

Agent 2

Customer Behaviour

Measures how far the payment departs from the customer's normal pattern.

Agent 3

Risk / Policy

Applies the bank's thresholds and safety floors, and cites only rules that actually fired.

Agent 4

Recommendation

Recommends clear, verify or hold, with up to three reasons that cite the evidence.

Every case follows one of three routes

A

Auto-clear

Low risk with complete data. Cleared and logged; one in three sampled for quality review.

H

Human review

Medium risk, missing data or suspicious text. The workflow pauses for a Fraud Analyst.

E

Escalation

High risk. Only a Senior Investigator can decide, checked inside the workflow itself.

Process and architecture

From the manual AS-IS process to the governed TO-BE process, and the system that runs it.

Guardrails and governance

No single control is trusted to stop every failure. Each one is mapped to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and ISO/IEC 27001:2022.

🔒

Privacy by design

Agents never see names or full account numbers. Models run locally, so evidence never leaves the machine.

ISO/IEC 27001 A.8.11 · NIST MAP 4
✓

Schema and evidence checks

Every reply is validated and checked against the real data. False claims are flagged; invalid replies get one retry, then go to a human.

NIST MEASURE 2.5, 2.9
⛔

Prompt-injection filter

Instructions hidden in payment remarks are removed before any model sees them, and the case cannot be auto-cleared.

NIST MEASURE 2.7 · ISO/IEC 27001 A.8.26
⚖

Policy floor

The final risk is the higher of the model's view and the rules. A model can raise risk, never lower it.

NIST MANAGE 1 · GOVERN 1.4
👤

Role-based access

Roles come from a user register, not a dropdown. Only Senior Investigators can decide escalated cases.

ISO/IEC 27001 A.5.15, A.5.18, A.8.2
📜

Full audit trail

Every sign-in, model call, retry, override and human decision (with its reason) is written to an append-only log.

ISO/IEC 27001 A.8.15 · NIST GOVERN 2

What we learned. Mistral 7B matched the policy on every case but was about four to five times slower. The smaller models mostly over-estimated risk: safe, because nothing risky was cleared, but costly, because it would flood senior investigators. The hard rules meant no model could ever clear a high-risk case.

Honest limits

  • All data is synthetic, and the 8 test cases show the design works, not real-world accuracy.
  • Rules and thresholds are illustrative, not a real bank's approved policy.
  • Sign-in is a demo name and PIN, not bank single sign-on. "Hold account" only records a decision.
